solution:
"""
URL: https://leetcode.com/problems/restore-ip-addresses/description/?envType=problem-list-v2&envId=vn57k9wr

93. Restore IP Addresses

A valid IP address consists of exactly four integers separated by single dots. Each integer is between 0 and 255 (inclusive) and cannot have leading zeros.

- For example, "0.1.2.201" and "192.168.1.1" are valid IP addresses, but "0.011.255.245", "192.168.1.312" and "192.168@1.1" are invalid IP addresses.

Given a string s containing only digits, return all possible valid IP addresses that can be formed by inserting dots into s. You are not allowed to reorder or remove any digits in s. You may return the valid IP addresses in any order.

Example 1:

Input: s = "25525511135"
Output: ["255.255.11.135","255.255.111.35"]

Example 2:

Input: s = "0000"
Output: ["0.0.0.0"]

Example 3:

Input: s = "101023"
Output: ["1.0.10.23","1.0.102.3","10.1.0.23","10.10.2.3","101.0.2.3"]

Constraints:

    1 <= s.length <= 20
    s consists of digits only.
"""


class Solution:
    def restoreIpAddresses(self, s: str) -> List[str]:
        res = []

        def backtrack(start: int, path: List[str]):
            if len(path) == 4:
                if start == len(s):
                    res.append(".".join(path))
                return

            if start == len(s):
                return

            for length in range(1, 4):
                if start + length > len(s):
                    break
                segment = s[start : start + length]
                # Check if segment is valid:
                # 1. no leading zeros unless single '0'
                # 2. integer value <= 255
                if (segment[0] == "0" and length > 1) or int(segment) > 255:
                    continue
                backtrack(start + length, path + [segment])

        backtrack(0, [])
        return res


sol = Solution()

print(sol.restoreIpAddresses("25525511135"))  # ["255.255.11.135","255.255.111.35"]

assert sorted(sol.restoreIpAddresses("25525511135")) == sorted(
    ["255.255.11.135", "255.255.111.35"]
)
assert sol.restoreIpAddresses("0000") == ["0.0.0.0"]
assert sorted(sol.restoreIpAddresses("101023")) == sorted(
    ["1.0.10.23", "1.0.102.3", "10.1.0.23", "10.10.2.3", "101.0.2.3"]
)

assert sorted(sol.restoreIpAddresses("1111")) == ["1.1.1.1"]
assert sorted(sol.restoreIpAddresses("010010")) == ["0.10.0.10", "0.100.1.0"]
assert sorted(sol.restoreIpAddresses("255255255255")) == ["255.255.255.255"]
assert sorted(sol.restoreIpAddresses("256256256256")) == []
assert sorted(sol.restoreIpAddresses("00000")) == []
assert sorted(sol.restoreIpAddresses("123")) == []
assert sorted(sol.restoreIpAddresses("12345678901234567890")) == []
assert sorted(sol.restoreIpAddresses("999999999999")) == []
assert sorted(sol.restoreIpAddresses("001001001001")) == []
assert sorted(sol.restoreIpAddresses("192168011")) == [
    "19.216.80.11",
    "192.16.80.11",
    "192.168.0.11",
]
assert sorted(sol.restoreIpAddresses("172162541")) == [
    "17.216.25.41",
    "17.216.254.1",
    "172.16.25.41",
    "172.16.254.1",
    "172.162.5.41",
    "172.162.54.1",
]
assert sorted(sol.restoreIpAddresses("000255000255")) == []
